paragraphs: Rabbi Yose Gelilaa, the Galilean. [Shabbat 46a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.46a.6) and [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.3.7.8) relate that he visited Rabbi Yose, son of Rabbi Chanina, and moved a lamp, to which Rabbi Yose bar Chanina objected. Hyman says he and Rabbi Yonah always transmitted teachings in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, as in [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, at the end of 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.3.1.25); [Kilayim, chapter 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.3.6.6); [Shabbat 7:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.4.2); and Nazir 6:1 in Hyman’s citation.[^2]

notes.text: The Galilean form is retained for this Amoraic notice; it is not silently identified with the Tanna Yose HaGelili. The prefixed kaf in the Kilayim chapter 3 reference is citation syntax, not a new section designation.

The linked Berakhot prints Yasa bar Chanina. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1945&lang=en) cites both the lamp incident and the joint transmission, and like the consulted text places the Nazir parallel at [7:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nazir.7.1.16).
